claims.text: The GPS trace is the governing measurement under POL-RD-01, and it records 54.16 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a platform optimal of 36.0 km — an excess of 18.16 km, or 50.44% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass (excess greater than 0.8 km AND greater than 20% of optimal), and the same excess also clears both materiality thresholds (8.0 km and 50%), so this deviation is ESTABLISHED and MATERIAL on this trip's own telemetry. I cite the trace figure, not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km, as POL-RD-01 requires.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 427 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps array and a max_gap_sec of 0.0 — comfortably inside the >90-second gap limb and the >30-second interval limb. The deviation therefore needs no independent corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) and can be established on the trace alone.

A material deviation triggers the driver-profile check under POL-RD-06. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 4, at or above the threshold of 3, so a repeat deviation pattern is ESTABLISHED. I disclose that this rests on EV-DPROF-00105, which the admissibility pre-pass tags IMPAIRED with weight_multiplier 0.75 and issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT (the snapshot is 108 hours before filed_at against a 72-hour threshold); the counter of 4 against a threshold of 3 survives that discount. I do not rely on prior_deviation_flags, which is a lifetime counter and not the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 names.

Because this deviation is both MATERIAL and substantiated on this trip's own evidence, POL-RD-06(b) licenses FULL_REFUND of charged_total rather than the POL-RD-02 partial. For auditability, the two figures side by side: under POL-RD-02 the charged_total is 65.13 and the recomputed_fare is 43.36, giving a partial of 21.80 (33.4% of the charge, well below the 90% full-refund share); the POL-RD-06(b) uplifted figure is the whole 65.13. There is no government-set or third-party pass-through line to carve out of the uplift: ERP is 0.00 and airport_surcharge is 0.00 — correctly, since this trip terminates at Changi and does not originate there.

The driver's statement that traffic was heavy on the PIE so he used another way names no advisory and no artifact. POL-RD-03 exoneration requires a traffic_advisory that names a road the optimal route traverses, with a validity window overlapping the trip. No such artifact exists: EV-ADVIS-00105-01 is MISSING, carries no payload, and has weight 0.0. Under POL-RD-08 a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by an advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden, and the traffic_advisory the clause requires is precisely what is absent.

The chat log contains no rider instruction to detour: two rider queries ('excuse me why are we going towards the city?' and 'we just passed bedok, my flight is at 5.15') and a single non-answer from the driver ('reaching soon'). Every message carries waypoint_hint null and the rider names no road, so the POL-RD-04 corroboration test cannot be run on the record, the clause is unavailable, and nothing in the chat reduces the excess.

Nothing on the trip record relocates the endpoints: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot re-baseline the optimal route to a longer amended one. The excess stands as measured against the booked 36.0 km optimal.

vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply and the baseline for the threshold test is the standard 36.0 km optimal — not a matched-itinerary figure and not a solo figure. The 18.16 km excess is charged against an unjustified detour, not against a pooled itinerary.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is met: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the same trip identifier TRP-00105 and the same 14:26-14:27 booking window, and the excess is measured from an unimpaired trace. The rider profile is clean — deviation_claims_60d is 0 — so no additional corroboration beyond the trace is required under the 30% rule for this claim.

claims.text: I do not dispute that the trace measures an excess, and I will not pretend otherwise: EV-GPS-00105 records 54.16 km of driven trace against the booked optimal of 36.0 km, an excess of 18.16 km that clears both POL-RD-01 gates (20% of optimal, 0.8 km absolute) and is on the numbers material. But that finding does one thing only — it opens the distance-and-time refund route on the booked-optimal comparison. It does not fix the size of the refund, and it does not by itself carry the rider to the whole fare he has asked for.

On the merits the policy supplies an arithmetic remedy, and it yields a partial refund, not the fare the rider demanded. charged_total of 65.13 less the recomputed optimal-route fare of 43.36 leaves 21.80 payable on the metered model with surge at 1.0 read from the fare breakdown. That is 33.4% of the charge, far below the 90% line at which POL-RD-02 replaces a partial with a full refund, and it is consistent with the rider's own estimate of 'about $44' for the journey he expected. The rider's demand for 'the entire fare, not a partial adjustment' overshoots the clause, and no clause in this policy pays delay damages for the check-in he feared missing.

The pass-through lines give the rider nothing further to stack. EV-FARE-00105 carries zero ERP gantry charges and a zero airport surcharge line, and that zero is correct rather than a defect: the Changi surcharge attaches only to trips ORIGINATING at the airport and this trip terminates there, so a surcharge line here would be the billing-integrity failure and its absence is proper. POL-RD-09(1) is the anti-double-count rule — off-route ERP is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 figure and must never be added on top of it — and with the ERP total at 0.00 there is nothing of that kind to add in any event.

The only foundation for converting the 21.80 partial into a 65.13 full refund is the driver-profile counter under POL-RD-06, and that artifact is impaired. EV-DPROF-00105 carries issue STALE_SNAPSHOT — snapshot_at is 108 hours before the dispute was filed, against a 72 hour threshold — and an admissibility weight of 0.75. I disclose that impairment as POL-GEN-02(1) requires rather than presenting the counter as current, and POL-GEN-02(2) caps the confidence the uplift can carry at the weight of the artifact that carries it. POL-RD-06(b) 'licenses' a full refund; it does not compel one. A trailing-90-day counter reading 4 flags, captured four and a half days before the filing and showing a rate of 4 in 344 completed trips, is a thin foundation for inflating the remedy to the maximum, and the finding that survives the discount should not be allowed to swell the money.

In the alternative, the record does not settle the driver's exculpation and the case belongs with a human reviewer. The driver's only account is that PIE traffic was heavy and he used another way, and the artifact that would test that account is absent from the bundle: EV-ADVIS-00105-01 is a MISSING traffic advisory with no payload and weight 0.0, and on its own face no LTA advisory covers the PIE eastbound in the 14:26-15:44 window on 15 July 2026. POL-RD-03 cannot be run against an advisory that does not exist, and POL-RD-10(5) makes precisely this posture — a congestion or closure assertion with no covering traffic advisory — a mandatory escalation trigger, with the escalation terminal and the disputed amount held rather than collected or refunded while a human reviews it. Absence of proof of the driver's explanation is a data failure, not a finding for the rider, and it should route the case to review rather than to a monetary ruling against the driver.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on the central measurement, and so do I. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00105) records 54.16 km between the recorded pickup and the recorded dropoff against the platform's optimal route of 36.0 km — an excess of 18.16 km, or 50.44% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass (more than 0.8 km and more than 20% of optimal) and both materiality tests pass (more than 8.0 km and more than 50%), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED and MATERIAL. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 427 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps list and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. It therefore stands on its own and needs no independent corroboration. I have measured the excess from the trace figure rather than the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km, as POL-RD-01 requires.

On the money. charged_total is 65.13. Recomputing the fare on the optimal route under POL-RD-02 — (3.80 base + 0.75 x 36.0 km + 0.28 x 42.0 min) x the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00105) + 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, no tolls and no airport surcharge — gives a recomputed_fare of 43.36. The ordinary POL-RD-02 refund is therefore 65.13 - 43.36 = 21.77, rounded up to 21.80 payable. The driver's arithmetic on that figure is correct, and the rider's demand for the whole fare is not something POL-RD-02 on its own supports.

But POL-RD-06 applies, and it changes the remedy. A material deviation triggers the driver-profile check. EV-DPROF-00105 records deviation_flags_90d of 4, at or above the threshold of 3, so a repeat deviation pattern is established. Because this deviation is both material and substantiated on this trip's own evidence, POL-RD-06(b) replaces the POL-RD-02 partial of 21.80 with FULL_REFUND of charged_total, 65.13. There is no pass-through line to carve out of the uplift: ERP is 0.00 and no airport surcharge is chargeable, because the Changi surcharge attaches only to trips ORIGINATING at the airport and this trip ended there — the zero line is correct, and a surcharge line here would have been the billing-integrity defect rather than the reverse. POL-RD-09 accordingly yields nothing to add on top of the refund.

The driver's point about the profile is well taken in part. EV-DPROF-00105 is impaired: it carries issue code STALE_SNAPSHOT (its snapshot is 108 hours before the dispute was filed, against a 72-hour threshold) and an admissibility weight of 0.75. The counter of 4 against a threshold of 3 survives that discount, so the pattern stands and the FULL_REFUND uplift follows — but the impairment caps the confidence of this ruling at 0.75, and that is the confidence I have set. POL-RD-06(b) does not give me a discretion to withhold the uplift once the pattern is established; the discount limits how much weight the ruling can claim, not whether the remedy is due. I have not used prior_deviation_flags, which is a lifetime counter, or any other profile field, none of which may carry a finding about this trip.

The driver's explanation that PIE traffic was heavy is a general assertion that names no traffic advisory and cites no artifact. Under POL-RD-08 such an assertion does not discharge the driver's burden of pointing to a specific exculpatory artifact, so it does not excuse the deviation; it also does not turn the case into a mandatory escalation, because no exculpatory clause was invoked against a cited artifact that is missing or unhelpful — the account stands alone. I have also confirmed the remaining clauses: nothing relocates the pickup or dropoff point (POL-RD-05 — both amendment timestamps and amended_optimal_distance_km are null), no rider instruction to detour appears in the chat log (POL-RD-04 — the messages are two rider queries and a non-answer, all with waypoint_hint null), and the trip is not pooled (POL-RD-12 — vehicle_type is RYDE_X), so the 36.0 km optimal is the correct baseline.

Finally, because a repeat deviation pattern is established, POL-RD-06(c) refers this case to driver-conduct review. That referral rides with the money and neither delays nor displaces it.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is the 15 July 2026 Jurong East to Changi T1 trip (TRP-00105), charged at SGD 65.13. The GPS trace does show a real and material route deviation, but the driver's explanation for it cannot be tested on this record. Under POL-RD-10 the case goes to a human reviewer and the SGD 65.13 is held — neither collected nor refunded — until it can be decided. Escalation is terminal and replaces any monetary ruling.

What is established. EV-GPS-00105 records 54.16 km driven between the recorded pickup and the recorded dropoff against the platform optimal of 36.0 km on EV-TRIP-00105: an excess of 18.16 km, 50.44% of optimal. That clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (over 0.8 km, over 20%) and both materiality thresholds (over 8.0 km, over 50%), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED and MATERIAL. I use the trace figure, not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km. The trace is NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 427 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0 — so no corroboration is needed for the deviation itself.

Why the case cannot be finally decided (POL-RD-10(5)). The driver's only account is 'traffic was heavy on the PIE so I used another way'. That is an exculpatory explanation turning on the road conditions, and the artifact the policy requires to test it — a traffic_advisory under POL-RD-03, naming a road the optimal route uses over the trip window — is absent from the bundle: EV-ADVIS-00105-01 is a MISSING artifact with no payload and weight 0.0. An exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool is a mandatory escalation trigger under POL-RD-10(5), which names this exact posture ('a closure asserted with no traffic_advisory'). Both advocates argued the advisory point, but the referee discarded each of those claims for citing the 0.0-weight artifact without disclosing its impairment and issue code (MISSING_ARTIFACT); the trigger therefore rests on the clause and the record alone, not on any advocate claim.

What would resolve it. The LTA traffic advisory — or any independent record of the road conditions — for the PIE eastbound and the alternative corridor actually driven, between 14:26 and 15:44 on 15 July 2026. With that artifact in the pool, POL-RD-03 could be run or dismissed and the fare question decided.

Points the reviewer will need. (a) No rider-requested detour: EV-CHAT-00105 carries no detour instruction and every message has waypoint_hint null, so POL-RD-04 cannot be run. (b) No endpoint amendment: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, so POL-RD-05 does not apply. (c) vehicle_type is RYDE_X, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. (d) No pass-through lines: ERP is 0.00 and the airport surcharge is 0.00 (correctly — the trip terminates at Changi and does not originate there). (e) On the money otherwise in issue: charged_total 65.13; POL-RD-02 recomputed_fare 43.36 (base 3.80 + 0.75 x 36.0 km + 0.28 x 42.0 min, surge 1.0 read from EV-FARE-00105, + 0.80 platform fee); POL-RD-02 partial 21.80. (f) A repeat-deviation pattern is established under POL-RD-06 — deviation_flags_90d = 4 against a threshold of 3 — on EV-DPROF-00105, which is impaired (STALE_SNAPSHOT: snapshot 108 hours before the filing against a 72-hour threshold) at weight multiplier 0.75; the counter survives that discount, and I do not use prior_deviation_flags, a lifetime counter that is context-only under POL-GEN-01. (g) The rider's own profile is clean and was not used against him. Confidence is capped at 0.75, the weight of the impaired profile that carries the pattern finding.

Every message carries waypoint_hint null and the rider names no road, so the POL-RD-04 corroboration test cannot be run on the record, the clause is unavailable, and nothing in the chat reduces the excess.

Nothing on the trip record relocates the endpoints: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot re-baseline the optimal route to a longer amended one. The excess stands as measured against the booked 36.0 km optimal.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is met: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry the same trip identifier TRP-00105 and the same 14:26-14:27 booking window, and the excess is measured from an unimpaired trace. The rider profile is clean — deviation_claims_60d is 0 — so no additional corroboration beyond the trace is required under the 30% rule for this claim.

I do not dispute that the trace measures an excess, and I will not pretend otherwise: EV-GPS-00105 records 54.16 km of driven trace against the booked optimal of 36.0 km, an excess of 18.16 km that clears both POL-RD-01 gates (20% of optimal, 0.8 km absolute) and is on the numbers material. But that finding does one thing only — it opens the distance-and-time refund route on the booked-optimal comparison. It does not fix the size of the refund, and it does not by itself carry the rider to the whole fare he has asked for.

EV-FARE-00105 carries zero ERP gantry charges and a zero airport surcharge line, and that zero is correct rather than a defect: the Changi surcharge attaches only to trips ORIGINATING at the airport and this trip terminates there, so a surcharge line here would be the billing-integrity failure and its absence is proper. POL-RD-09(1) is the anti-double-count rule — off-route ERP is already comprehended in the POL-RD-02 figure and must never be added on top of it — and with the ERP total at 0.00 there is nothing of that kind to add in any event.

The only foundation for converting the 21.80 partial into a 65.13 full refund is the driver-profile counter under POL-RD-06, and that artifact is impaired. EV-DPROF-00105 carries issue STALE_SNAPSHOT — snapshot_at is 108 hours before the dispute was filed, against a 72 hour threshold — and an admissibility weight of 0.75. I disclose that impairment as POL-GEN-02(1) requires rather than presenting the counter as current, and POL-GEN-02(2) caps the confidence the uplift can carry at the weight of the artifact that carries it. POL-RD-06(b) 'licenses' a full refund; it does not compel one. A trailing-90-day counter reading 4 flags, captured four and a half days before the filing and showing a rate of 4 in 344 completed trips, is a thin foundation for inflating the remedy to the maximum, and the finding that survives the discount should not be allowed to swell the money.

In the alternative, the record does not settle the driver's exculpation and the case belongs with a human reviewer. The driver's only account is that PIE traffic was heavy and he used another way, and the artifact that would test that account is absent from the bundle: EV-ADVIS-00105-01 is a MISSING traffic advisory with no payload and weight 0.0, and on its own face no LTA advisory covers the PIE eastbound in the 14:26-15:44 window on 15 July 2026. POL-RD-03 cannot be run against an advisory that does not exist, and POL-RD-10(5) makes precisely this posture — a congestion or closure assertion with no covering traffic advisory — a mandatory escalation trigger, with the escalation terminal and the disputed amount held rather than collected or refunded while a human reviews it. Absence of proof of the driver's explanation is a data failure, not a finding for the rider, and it should route the case to review rather than to a monetary ruling against the driver.
